To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

plasma TG and NEFA concentrations in Zucker rats are dependent on plasma glucose and insulin concentrations and that YM268 improves insulin sensitivity with respect TG and NEFA but not glucose metabolism in obese rats.
insulin sensitivity with respect of TG and NEFA concentration in obese rats is not different from that in their lean littermates.
insulin sensitivity for glucose metabolism in obese Zucker rats is not different from that in their lean controls, but is different for lipid metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of insulin in the regulation of lipid metabolism in insulin resistant obese rats and the effect of a new insulin sensitizer, 2-(4-methanesulfonylphenyl)-5-(4-pyridinyl)-1H-imidazo[4,5-c]quinolin-4-one, YM268, on lipid and glucose metabolism in lean and insulin resistant obese Zucker rats.
the role of the endocrine pancreas and the role of insulin and insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) in the regulation of glucose homeostasis, insulin resistance, and diabetes.
the regulation of plasma lipid metabolism by insulin in Zucker rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin is not a key player in regulating glucose metabolism in obese Zucker rats, but it is a key player in lipid metabolism.
plasma TG and NEFA concentrations are insulin-dependent in Zucker rats and insulin resistance is not a factor in this regard.
insulin is not a major determinant of plasma lipid levels, but it is a major determinant for plasma glucose level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasma insulin regulates plasma lipid concentration in lean and obese rat models.
insulin resistance in obese Zucker rats does not seem to be due to impaired insulin sensitivity for glucose, TG, or NEFA metabolism.

the plasma insulin concentration is the primary determinant of plasma lipid levels in both lean and obese Zucker rat, and that insulin resistance is not a major factor contributing to the elevated plasma lipid levels in obese Zucker rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plasma TG and NEFA are regulated by insulin, and the sensitivity of obese Zucker rats is not different from that of lean Zucker rats.

plasma insulin concentration regulates glucose and lipid metabolism and insulin resistance in the obese Zucker rat model is not due to a defect in insulin sensitivity with respect lipid and TG metabolism.

plasma TG concentration in lean and obese animals is dependent on plasma insulin concentration, and insulin sensitivity in obese animals with respect to TG metabolism may not be different than that in lean animals.
